campaign_objective: Implement and verify every capability-boundary report intent in Lilies; all stage, contract, test, archive, and evidence mechanisms are subordinate to this outcome.
priority_rule: latest_user_instruction > report_campaign_and_intent_registry > stage_report_sequence > stage_contract > current_design > working_evidence

intents.statement: Keep model intelligence as the primary requirement-understanding, planning, workflow-composition, and repair mechanism.
intents.acceptance: Builder behavior and product flows do not reduce complex requirements to fixed templates when model reasoning is available.

intents.statement: Separate workflow-internal Harness blocks, Evaluation Harness, and Platform Harness in data contracts, UI labels, and claims.
intents.acceptance: Users and engineers can identify which layer owns each control; no generic Harness label conflates all three.

intents.statement: Provide coexisting Quick, Guided, and Governed workflow construction and operation modes.
intents.acceptance: Simple low-risk requirements can reach a runnable workflow without mandatory heavy acceptance; higher-risk workflows can opt into stronger evidence and controls.

intents.statement: Make acceptance advisory for Quick and Guided modes while preserving explicit governed hard-policy gates.
intents.acceptance: A user can publish with visible warnings in Quick/Guided mode; a configured Governed policy can still deny publication with an explicit reason.

intents.statement: Turn failed acceptance cases into actionable repair suggestions and a one-click Builder Team workflow-edit preview.
intents.acceptance: A failed case exposes structured advice and can open a natural-language workflow edit preview carrying the relevant workflow, node, trace, and failure context.

intents.statement: Expose human-readable, schema-driven configuration for common blocks and keep raw JSON as an expert view.
intents.acceptance: LLM, HTTP/tool, and Loop blocks can be configured through purpose-built controls whose saved values change the canonical WorkflowSpec and runtime behavior.

intents.statement: Invalidate acceptance evidence after behavior-affecting workflow edits and recommend revalidation without deleting publication choice.
intents.acceptance: Editing behavior changes tested evidence to stale, displays what changed, and offers revalidation while keeping the draft usable.

intents.statement: Separate Customer Runtime, Engineer Studio, and Governance Console information architectures.
intents.acceptance: Customer runtime does not expose engineering JSON or platform internals; Studio retains workflow engineering; governance is available outside one application detail page.

intents.statement: Make reusable workflow modules and verified templates first-class capability carriers.
intents.acceptance: A versioned module declares inputs, outputs, dependencies, envelope, evidence, and known boundaries and can be selected by Builder Team.

intents.statement: Model requirements as functional capabilities, runtime guarantees, and external contracts (F/G/X).
intents.acceptance: Codex-like, scheduled crawler, and customer-embedded scenarios produce materially different typed F/G/X closures while retaining original natural language.

intents.statement: Represent capability dependencies, requires/excludes relationships, required execution envelope, and environment availability.
intents.acceptance: Capability closure is deterministic, missing dependencies are explicit, and unavailable external contracts are not misreported as workflow defects.

intents.statement: Choose a capability carrier before adding a block: atomic block, reusable module, runtime/platform service, hard platform control, or connector/external contract.
intents.acceptance: Builder output records the selected carrier and rationale; a capability is not automatically converted into a new atomic block.

intents.statement: Produce a Capability Build Contract from Builder Team.
intents.acceptance: Builder output contains target capabilities, envelope, external contracts, platform coverage, evidence plan, carrier choices, and claim scope.

intents.statement: Use E0-E5 as cumulative execution envelopes while keeping risk and functional capability orthogonal.
intents.acceptance: Routing and claims distinguish one-shot cognition, stateful workflow, tool loop, durable task, governed automation, and production embedding without treating them as one keyword complexity score.

intents.statement: Make structured Loop/Subflow semantics first class without opening unrestricted cyclic graphs.
intents.acceptance: Loop exposes state, condition, max iterations, break, cancel, checkpoint, and per-iteration trace with tool-result feedback.

intents.statement: Build a durable job substrate for timer/event triggers, history, retry, resume, idempotency, leases, cancellation, and alerts.
intents.acceptance: A scheduled workflow survives process restart, avoids duplicate fire, records history, resumes or fails explicitly, and can be cancelled.

intents.statement: Provide a Connector/Embedding SDK for identity, tenants, schemas, callbacks, writeback, compensation, and deployment profiles.
intents.acceptance: A customer-system integration can be implemented against a versioned contract without embedding customer-specific logic in generic HTTP blocks.

intents.statement: Make Evaluation Harness profiles selectable and capable of H0-H5 evidence levels.
intents.acceptance: Users or policy select whether and how far evaluation runs; results state design, static, component, contract, live, or production evidence without conflation.

intents.statement: Represent component_verified, integration_verified, live_verified, blocked_by_environment, design_only, and unsupported states.
intents.acceptance: Unavailable customer environments produce a scoped status and contract gap instead of forced pass/fail or fabricated evidence.

intents.statement: Generate tests from capability signals, runtime envelope, external contracts, and selected evidence level.
intents.acceptance: Loop, tool, scheduler, customer writeback, and high-risk workflows generate different tests and evidence requirements.

intents.statement: Provide mock, contract, sandbox, live, and production-observation evaluation environments.
intents.acceptance: Each test case identifies its environment and evidence level; claim scope cannot exceed the strongest completed evidence.

intents.statement: Create an independent Governance Console for cross-application tasks, policies, workers, queues, failures, and parent-child traces.
intents.acceptance: Governance data is reachable outside an application detail page and can filter and drill into platform tasks.

intents.statement: Record and visualize input, output, cached, and reasoning tokens plus cost and remaining budget over time.
intents.acceptance: Token and cost series can be queried by time, model, workflow, application, and owner with explicit unsupported fields.

intents.statement: Build a Capability Evidence Registry linking implementation, defaults, API, tests, live evidence, telemetry, gaps, and claim level.
intents.acceptance: Every platform capability claim can be queried and traced to evidence; missing token limits cannot be described as implemented by call-count approximation.

intents.statement: Add domain-aware high-risk autonomy governance with preauthorization, emergency stop, audit, and production exercises.
intents.acceptance: High-risk autonomy is enabled only for a declared domain and cannot bypass configured hard controls.

intents.statement: Use a Codex-like workflow as an E2/E3 capability-closure and tool-feedback-loop acceptance scenario.
intents.acceptance: The generated editable workflow exposes context, planning, tools, permission boundaries, feedback loop, stop conditions, trace, and user-facing result flow.

intents.statement: Use a daily web collection workflow as the E3 durable scheduling pressure scenario.
intents.acceptance: The scenario covers schedule, dedupe, pagination/loop, source provenance, storage, notification, retry, resume, cancel, and explicit site-access contract.

intents.statement: Use customer-system embedding as the E4/E5 connector, identity, writeback, compensation, and evidence pressure scenario.
intents.acceptance: A mock or test tenant proves the component/contract boundary, and the product refuses to claim end-to-end production success without a real environment.

intents.statement: Keep Program Charter as an immutable intent constraint and stage reports as the only next-task authority.
intents.acceptance: Validators reject a stage report with unknown source intents or a next task without a stable task ID; workingon contains no authoritative next-stage task set.

intents.statement: Freeze a mandatory/optional Stage Contract before implementation.
intents.acceptance: A version cannot close while any mandatory task lacks completed evidence or a user-approved contract revision.

intents.statement: Use a deterministic Closure Audit and stable intent coverage to prevent self-declared or summary-only completion.
intents.acceptance: Closure validation finds missing mandatory tasks, disappearing intent IDs, unsupported claims, stale evidence, and invalid version advancement.

intents.statement: Classify implementation, substitution, scope, and safety deviations with explicit authority.
intents.acceptance: Implementation changes can proceed with records; scope or acceptance changes cannot proceed without user decision.

intents.statement: Resume long work from the current Stage Contract and task ID after interruption or context compaction.
intents.acceptance: Startup/resume checks load charter, stage contract, task ID, evidence, and git status before new planning; an open mandatory task is continued rather than replaced.

intents.statement: Advance versions only for coherent vertical capability, complete experiment, process-architecture repair, or explicit hotfix exception.
intents.acceptance: Repeated one-design and prerequisite-only versions fail the version advancement validator; major versions archive their complete stage-report set.

intents.statement: Separate implementation completion from external evidence availability and preserve unavailable higher evidence as scoped debt.
intents.acceptance: An unavailable browser, model, tool, customer environment, or live integration records blocked_by_environment, achieved level, claim ceiling, and recheck trigger without stopping unrelated report work or fabricating a pass.

intents.statement: Permit campaign-wide blocking only when every remaining authorized report-intent route is blocked.
intents.acceptance: Validators and resume hooks preserve the report campaign as highest priority, reject stage-local evidence-provider self-blocking, and prevent repeated unchanged external probes from replacing implementation progress.
